scenes.narration: Traditionally, every network job needed its own special box. A router box, a firewall box, a load balancer box. N F V turns them into software.

lines.t: A router box, a firewall box

scenes.heading: From appliances to apps
scenes.narration: Think of swapping a drawer full of gadgets for apps on one phone. Network functions run as software on ordinary servers. The servers and hypervisor underneath are the N F V I. M A N O is the manager that starts, stops and scales them. Virtual routers and firewalls are common examples.

scenes.heading: Common mix-ups
scenes.narration: Three tips. Ordinary servers do the job. N F V virtualises functions, and S D N separates control. M A N O manages, it doesn't forward.

items.wrong: NFV and SDN are the same

scenes.heading: Remember this
scenes.narration: So, to recap. N F V turns network boxes into software. Three parts: N F V I, V N F and M A N O. It runs on ordinary servers. Ready to practise? Try the Courseiva NFV lab.
